claim_after: Your body needs about 0.1 mg of folate each day, and the stores in your body can last for only 3–4 months, so severe folate deficiency can develop quickly if not replenished.

claim_after: Acetaminophen is an alternative in patients with a history of GI bleeding and can be used safely at up to 4 g/d given in four doses of 1000 mg each.

claim_after: Acetazolamide (250 to 0.5 g) can be given orally or intravenously two to four times daily to induce renal bicarbonate diuresis.
